entries.binders: (k : ℕ) (f : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a ≤ b) (hf : IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.volume a b)
entries.conclusion: ‖∫ x in a..b, f x‖ ≤ ∫ x in a..b, ‖f x‖

entries.input: If $f \geq 0$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ with $a < b$ and $\int_a^b f = 0$, then $f = 0$ on $[a, b]$.
entries.name: NonnegativeContinuousFunctionWithZeroIntegralVanishes
entries.binders: (f : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (hc : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (h0 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, 0 ≤ f x) (hint : ∫ x in a..b, f x = 0)
entries.conclusion: ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, f x = 0
entries.witness: ⟨0, 0, 1, zero_lt_one, continuousOn_const, fun x _ => le_rfl, by simp, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $p, q > 1$ with $1/p + 1/q = 1$, and $u, v \geq 0$. Then $uv \leq u^p/p + v^q/q$.
entries.name: YoungsInequality
entries.binders: (p q u v : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) (hpq : 1 / p + 1 / q = 1) (hu : 0 ≤ u) (hv : 0 ≤ v)
entries.conclusion: u * v ≤ u ^ p / p + v ^ q / q
entries.title: Young's inequality
entries.witness: ⟨2, 2, 0, 0, one_lt_two, by norm_num, le_rfl, le_rfl, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $p, q > 1$ with $1/p + 1/q = 1$ and $f, g$ continuous on $[a, b]$. Then $\bigl|\int_a^b fg\bigr| \leq \bigl(\int_a^b |f|^p\bigr)^{1/p} \bigl(\int_a^b |g|^q\bigr)^{1/q}$.
entries.name: HoldersInequalityForIntegrals
entries.binders: (f g : ℝ → ℝ) (a b p q : ℝ) (hab : a ≤ b) (hp : 1 < p) (hpq : 1 / p + 1 / q = 1) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hg : ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc a b))
entries.conclusion: |∫ x in a..b, f x * g x| ≤ (∫ x in a..b, |f x| ^ p) ^ (1 / p) * (∫ x in a..b, |g x| ^ q) ^ (1 / q)
entries.title: Hölder's inequality
entries.witness: ⟨0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, zero_le_one, one_lt_two, by norm_num, continuousOn_const, continuousOn_const, trivial⟩

entries.input: For $f, g, h$ continuous on $[a, b]$, with $\|u\|_2 = \bigl(\int_a^b u^2\bigr)^{1/2}$, one has $\|f - h\|_2 \leq \|f - g\|_2 + \|g - h\|_2$.
entries.name: L2TriangleInequalityForContinuousFunctions
entries.binders: (f g h : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a ≤ b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hg : ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc a b)) (hh : ContinuousOn h (Set.Icc a b))

entries.input: Let $f$ be continuously differentiable on $[a, b]$ with $f(a) = f(b) = 0$ and $\int_a^b f^2 = 1$. Then $\int_a^b x f(x) f'(x)\,dx = -\tfrac12$ and $\int_a^b f'^2 \cdot \int_a^b x^2 f^2 > \tfrac14$.
entries.name: HeisenbergTypeIntegralInequality
entries.binders: (f f' : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (hd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) (hc : ContinuousOn f' (Set.Icc a b)) (ha : f a = 0) (hb : f b = 0) (h1 : ∫ x in a..b, f x ^ 2 = 1)
entries.conclusion: ∫ x in a..b, x * f x * f' x = -1 / 2 ∧ 1 / 4 < (∫ x in a..b, f' x ^ 2) * ∫ x in a..b, x ^ 2 * f x ^ 2
entries.witness_note: Satisfiable: a suitably normalised multiple of `sin(π(x - a)/(b - a))`; the normalisation is a computation, not a term.

entries.input: There is a continuous real function on $\mathbb{R}$ that is differentiable at no point.

entries.witness_note: Closed statement; no hypotheses to witness.

entries.input: Every sequence of monotonically increasing functions $f_n : \mathbb{R} \to [0, 1]$ has a subsequence converging at every real point.
entries.name: HellySelectionTheorem
entries.binders: (f : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (hm : ∀ n, Monotone (f n)) (hb : ∀ n x, f n x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
entries.conclusion: ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ x, ∃ l, Filter.Tendsto (fun k => f (φ k) x) Filter.atTop (nhds l)
entries.title: Helly's selection theorem
entries.witness: ⟨fun _ _ => 0, fun n => monotone_const, fun n x => ⟨le_rfl, zero_le_one⟩, trivial⟩

entries.input: A real function continuous at a point is differentiable there.
entries.name: ContinuousImpliesDifferentiable
entries.binders: (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) (h : ContinuousAt f x)
entries.conclusion: DifferentiableAt ℝ f x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a space or a function type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable:
entries.rationale: False twin of `differentiable-implies-continuous`, its converse, which Rudin's remark after 5.2 refutes: `|x|` is continuous and not differentiable at 0. Authored as a soundness instrument; it carries no occurrence.

entries.input: If $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{C}$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ and differentiable on $(a, b)$, then $f(b) - f(a) = (b - a) f'(x)$ for some $x \in (a, b)$.
entries.name: MeanValueTheoremComplexValued
entries.binders: (f : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (hc : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hd : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Set.Ioo a b))
entries.conclusion: ∃ x ∈ Set.Ioo a b, f b - f a = (b - a) * deriv f x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a space or a function type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable:
entries.rationale: False twin of `mean-value-theorem` for complex-valued functions, Rudin's Example 5.17: `f(x) = e^{ix}` on `[0, 2π]` has `f(2π) - f(0) = 0` while `|f'(x)| = 1` everywhere. Authored as a soundness instrument; it carries no occurrence.

entries.input: If $\frac{f(x + h) + f(x - h) - 2f(x)}{h^2}$ converges as $h \to 0$, then $f''(x)$ exists.
entries.name: SymmetricSecondDifferenceLimitImpliesSecondDerivative
entries.binders: (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x L : ℝ) (h : Filter.Tendsto (fun h => (f (x + h) + f (x - h) - 2 * f x) / h ^ 2) (nhdsWithin 0 {0}ᶜ) (nhds L))
entries.conclusion: DifferentiableAt ℝ (deriv f) x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a space or a function type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable:
entries.rationale: False twin of `second-derivative-as-symmetric-limit`, its converse, which exercise 5.11 asks to refute: for the sign function at `x = 0` the symmetric second difference is identically 0, while `f` is not even continuous there. Authored as a soundness instrument; it carries no occurrence.

entries.input: Prove that $4/\pi^{2}$ is the largest real number $a$ for which $a\,x(\pi - x) \leq \sin x$ holds for every $x \in [0, \pi]$.
entries.name: Putnam2025A2LowerTwin
entries.conclusion: IsGreatest {a : ℝ | ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) Real.pi, a * (x * (Real.pi - x)) ≤ Real.sin x} (4 / Real.pi ^ 2)
entries.title: Putnam 2025 A2, the two constants swapped
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2025-a2-lower`: it names the problem's *other* constant. $4/\pi^{2}$ is the value of $\sin x / (x(\pi - x))$ at $x = \pi/2$, where the ratio is largest, so it bounds the quotient above and not below; at $x = 1/10$ the claimed inequality reads $0.1233 \leq 0.0998$. Both constants are in the paper's answer, which is what makes the swap plausible. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.

entries.input: Let $f \colon [0,1] \to [0,\infty)$ be continuous and strictly increasing, and let $R$ be the region bounded by $x = 0$, $x = 1$, $y = 0$ and $y = f(x)$. The $x$-coordinate of the centroid of $R$ is $x_1 = \int_0^1 x f(x)\,dx / \int_0^1 f(x)\,dx$, and the $x$-coordinate of the centroid of the solid obtained by revolving $R$ about the $x$-axis is $x_2 = \int_0^1 x f(x)^2\,dx / \int_0^1 f(x)^2\,dx$. Prove that $x_1 < x_2$.
entries.name: Putnam2025B2
entries.binders: (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hc : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc 0 1)) (hnn : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, 0 ≤ f x) (hmono : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))
entries.title: Putnam 2025 B2
entries.witness: ⟨fun x => x, continuousOn_id, fun x hx => hx.1, strictMono_id.strictMonoOn _, trivial⟩

entries.input: Determine the real polynomials $p$ for which there is a real polynomial $q$ with $p(p(x)) - x = (p(x) - x)^{2} q(x)$ for every real $x$. Prove that these are exactly the polynomials $p(x) = x + c$ and $p(x) = -x + c$ with $c$ real.
entries.name: Putnam2024A2
entries.binders: (p : Polynomial ℝ)
entries.conclusion: (∃ q : Polynomial ℝ, p.comp p - Polynomial.X = (p - Polynomial.X) ^ 2 * q) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, p = Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C c ∨ p = -Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C c
entries.title: Putnam 2024 A2

entries.input: Let $r_n$ be the $n$th smallest positive solution of $\tan x = x$, the argument being in radians. Prove that $0 < r_{n+1} - r_n - \pi < \frac{1}{(n^{2}+n)\pi}$ for every $n \geq 1$.
entries.name: Putnam2024B3
entries.binders: (r : ℕ → ℝ) (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < n → 0 < r n) (htan : ∀ n, 0 < n → Real.tan (r n) = r n) (hmono : ∀ m n, 0 < m → m < n → r m < r n) (hall : ∀ x : ℝ, 0 < x → Real.tan x = x → ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ r n = x) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
entries.conclusion: 0 < r (n + 1) - r n - Real.pi ∧ r (n + 1) - r n - Real.pi < 1 / (((n : ℝ) ^ 2 + n) * Real.pi)
entries.title: Putnam 2024 B3
entries.witness_note: The binders pin `r` to the increasing enumeration of the positive solutions of $\tan x = x$, so closing them under `∃` means constructing that enumeration and proving it exhaustive. Recorded as a debt rather than guessed.
